title: Cuff Craft
summary: A playable bio-quest demo: meet through effort, not a swipe.

blocks.title: The bio is the quest giver.
blocks.body: No pickup line. No swipe queue. A little thought opens a different kind of door.

blocks.heading: Do the quest. Earn the conversation.
blocks.description: Choose a fictional profile. Their bio gives you a writing quest. Your answer becomes the introduction, not a swipe.

profiles.name: Rowan, 28
profiles.bio: I fix bikes, collect terrible postcards, and take the long way home. Tell me about something you care enough to notice.
profiles.interests: Bike rides / tiny museums / bad puns
profiles.prompt: You have one free afternoon and $20. Plan a small adventure for two strangers. What would we do, and why does it matter to you?
profiles.hint: A place, one surprising detail, and something about you. No perfect answer required.
profiles.reply: The tiny-adventure idea got me. What is the first stop you would actually choose?

profiles.name: Mila, 30
profiles.bio: Weekend baker. Amateur birdwatcher. I would rather hear about a real mistake than a perfect life.
profiles.prompt: Tell me about a time you were bad at something and kept trying. What changed, and what are you still learning?
profiles.hint: Pick one real moment. A small story beats a list of achievements.
profiles.reply: I like that you stayed with it. What would you tell yourself on that first day?

profiles.name: Ellis, 27
profiles.bio: Bookstore regular. Board-game host. I think the best conversations start with a question nobody expected.
profiles.prompt: Invent a tiny museum with only three objects from everyday life. What goes in it, and what story do those objects tell?
profiles.hint: Name the objects, then connect them. Odd is welcome. Thoughtful is the point.
profiles.reply: I would visit that museum. Which object would you put right by the entrance?

blocks.title: A quest opens a door, not a right to someone.
blocks.body: In a real product, the other person decides whether to accept your introduction. This demo lets you try both sides. A word count cannot judge sincerity or detect AI-written answers. No message leaves this page, no account is needed, and nothing is saved after you reload.

blocks.heading: Writing first. The world later.
blocks.body: This is the smallest loop: profile, quest, introduction, consent, conversation. Local scavenger hunts and real-world loot could follow. This demo does not promise prizes, real matches, or a live dating service.
